title: CyberShield: Escape the Hacker's Trap
description: A mysterious hacker has locked down your school's digital systems! Navigate through three secure rooms -- the Phishing Lab, Password Vault, and Social Media HQ -- to restore safety. Solve puzzles about online threats, crack weak passwords, and fix privacy settings before time runs out!
learning_objectives: Identify phishing emails and social engineering tactics
Understand what makes passwords strong vs weak
Learn essential social media privacy settings and digital hygiene
Develop critical thinking about online threats and digital safety

how_to_play.title: How to Play
steps: Explore each room by examining the clues -- tap on emails, documents, and objects to read them
Use the clues to piece together information needed to solve each room's puzzle
Answer the puzzle question correctly to unlock the next room
Progress through the Phishing Lab, Password Vault, and Social Media HQ
Complete all three rooms before the 5-minute timer runs out to escape!
tips: Read every clue carefully -- some contain hints that are crucial for solving the puzzle
Look for red flags like mismatched domains, urgency language, and suspicious links
If you get stuck, re-read the clues -- the answer is always hidden in the details

rooms.title: The Phishing Lab
rooms.description: You enter a room full of screens showing incoming emails. The hacker has mixed real emails with dangerous phishing attempts. You need to identify the fakes to unlock the next room!

clues.label: Suspicious Email #1
clues.content:
FROM: security@paytm-verify-account.com
SUBJECT: URGENT: Your Paytm Account Will Be Suspended!

Dear User,
We detected unusual activity on your account. Click the link below IMMEDIATELY to verify your identity or your account will be permanently deleted in 24 hours.

[VERIFY NOW: http://paytm-secure-login.suspicious-site.ru/verify]

Paytm Security Team
clues.hint: Look carefully at the sender's email domain and the link URL. Do they match the real Paytm website?

clues.label: Comparison: Real Paytm Email
clues.content:
FROM: noreply@paytm.com
SUBJECT: Your Paytm Monthly Statement

Hi Rahul,
Here is your monthly account summary. You can view details by logging into the Paytm app.

This is an automated email. Do not reply.
Paytm

clues.label: Phishing Red Flags Poster
clues.content:
SPOT THE PHISH -- Red Flags Checklist:
1. Sender domain doesn't match the company (e.g., @paytm-verify.com instead of @paytm.com)
2. Creates URGENCY or FEAR ('account deleted in 24 hours!')
3. Asks you to click suspicious links
4. Generic greeting ('Dear User' instead of your name)
5. Spelling/grammar mistakes
6. Threatens negative consequences if you don't act NOW

puzzles.question: Which red flags confirm that Email #1 is a phishing attempt? Choose the BEST answer.
options: Wrong domain (@paytm-verify-account.com), creates urgency, generic greeting, suspicious link with .ru domain
The email has too many capital letters
Paytm never sends emails to anyone
The email was sent at night time
puzzles.explanation: The fake domain, urgency tactics, generic 'Dear User' greeting, and a suspicious .ru link are classic phishing red flags. Real companies use their official domain and address you by name. Never click links in suspicious emails -- go to the app directly!

rooms.title: The Password Vault
rooms.description: The hacker's screen shows a list of cracked passwords from your school. The vault door needs the strongest password to unlock. Analyse which passwords are weak and figure out what makes a password truly secure!

clues.label: Hacker's Cracked Password List
clues.content:
PASSWORDS CRACKED IN UNDER 1 SECOND:
- password123
- rahul2008
- ilovecricket
- 12345678
- qwerty
- india@123

PASSWORDS THAT TOOK 3+ YEARS TO CRACK:
- Tr!cky_M0ng00se#42
- Kh!chd!_P@neer$99
- B1ue_T!ger_Runs@Dawn
clues.hint: What do the strong passwords have that the weak ones don't? Look at length, special characters, and patterns.

clues.label: Password Strength Guide
clues.content:
STRONG PASSWORD RECIPE:
- At least 12 characters long
- Mix of UPPERCASE and lowercase
- Include numbers (0-9)
- Include special characters (!@#$%)
- NOT a real word or your name/birthday
- NOT a common pattern (123, qwerty, abcd)

PRO TIP: Use a passphrase! Take a sentence and modify it:
'I love butter chicken on Sundays' becomes 'iLuv_Butt3r_Ch!ck3n_0n_$undays'

puzzles.question: The vault door needs the STRONGEST password to open. Which one should you enter?
puzzles.explanation: The third option is strongest because it has 26+ characters, mixes cases, uses special characters (#$!), replaces letters with numbers (7h3, Qu!ck, Br0wn, F0x), and isn't a predictable pattern. 'MySchool@2024' uses personal info, 'P@ssw0rd' is a known variant hackers test first, and 'ILoveMango123!' follows a predictable pattern.

rooms.title: Social Media HQ
rooms.description: Final room! The hacker exploited a student's public social media profile to gather personal information. Fix the privacy settings and identify what should NEVER be shared online to shut down the hacker for good!

clues.label: Exposed Student Profile
clues.content:
HACKER'S NOTES -- Data harvested from Priya's public Instagram:
- Full name: Priya Sharma
- School: DPS Bangalore, Class 10-B
- Birthday: March 15, 2010
- Location tags: Home (HSR Layout), School, Tuition centre
- Phone number in bio: +91 98XXX XXXXX
- Mom's name from tagged photos: 'Sunita Sharma'
- Pet name from posts: 'Bruno'

The hacker used this info to:
1. Guess her password (Bruno2010)
2. Answer security questions (Mother's maiden name, pet's name)
3. Track her daily routine from location tags
clues.hint: Think about which of these details could be used against her. What should be private?

clues.label: Digital Safety Poster
clues.content:
SOCIAL MEDIA SAFETY RULES:
1. Set profile to PRIVATE -- only approved followers see your posts
2. NEVER share: phone number, home address, school name, daily schedule
3. Disable location tagging on photos
4. Don't use real birthday/pet name/family names as passwords
5. Enable Two-Factor Authentication (2FA) on all accounts
6. Think before you post: 'Would I want a stranger to know this?'
7. Review tagged photos before they appear on your profile

clues.label: Sticky Note on Monitor
clues.content:
Two-Factor Authentication (2FA) means even if someone steals your password, they STILL can't log in without a second verification -- usually a code sent to your phone. Enable it on Instagram, Gmail, Snapchat, everything!

It's like having two locks on your door instead of one.

puzzles.question: What is the MOST important combination of actions to protect Priya's accounts right now?
options: Delete all social media accounts permanently
Set profile to private, remove personal info from bio, enable 2FA, change password to something not based on personal details
Just change the password to a stronger one
Block the hacker and keep posting normally
puzzles.explanation: A multi-layered approach is best! Setting the profile to private stops data harvesting, removing personal info from the bio cuts off easy reconnaissance, 2FA adds a second security layer, and a non-personal password prevents guessing. Deleting everything is overkill, just changing the password isn't enough, and blocking one hacker doesn't fix the root vulnerability.

win_conditions.description: Escape all 3 rooms before the 300-second timer runs out! Find clues, solve puzzles, and become a cybersecurity pro. The internet is safer with you on guard!

transfer_exercises.real_world: Making fast calls during a team project deadline crunch
transfer_exercises.challenge: Practice making a decision in under 60 seconds on something you've been procrastinating. Reflect on the outcome.

transfer_exercises.game_context: Recovering from mistakes in rapid gameplay
transfer_exercises.real_world: Bouncing back after a failed presentation or test
transfer_exercises.challenge: Write down one recent failure and three specific things you learned from it.

glossary_terms.definition: The mental effort required to process information and make decisions.
glossary_terms.example: Having too many options at once makes decisions harder and slower.
glossary_terms.deep_dive: Working memory has limits. Experts chunk information into patterns, reducing cognitive load and enabling faster decisions.
glossary_terms.real_world_example: Experienced doctors diagnose faster not because they think harder, but because they recognize patterns instantly.

glossary_terms.definition: Identifying recurring structures or relationships in information.
glossary_terms.example: Noticing that certain question types always have two plausible answers helps you focus faster.
glossary_terms.deep_dive: Pattern recognition is a core skill in chess, medicine, engineering, and sport. It develops through deliberate practice.
glossary_terms.real_world_example: Air traffic controllers recognize dangerous flight patterns faster than computers because of years of pattern training.

glossary_terms.definition: The ability to direct mental attention toward what matters most and ignore distractions.
glossary_terms.example: Under time pressure, completing questions you're confident about before tackling harder ones.
glossary_terms.deep_dive: Focus is a trainable skill. The Pomodoro method, mindfulness, and deliberate practice all improve sustained attention.
glossary_terms.real_world_example: Olympic athletes train mental focus as rigorously as physical skills — pressure performance depends on it.

coaching_moment: If you get something wrong, reset and continue. Resilience isn't about never failing — it's about how quickly you get back on track.
cultural_context: India produces more software engineers than any other country, yet employability in technology remains a challenge due to skills gaps. CyberShield: Escape the Hacker's Trap builds the logical and computational thinking that is foundational for India's tech workforce.
reflection_prompt: What pattern did you start to recognize as you played? How will you use it next time?
